messages:
pagerduty-bot: 🔔 PagerDuty: Service 'inference-api' HIGH - Triggered by alert 'canary_response_error_rate' -> https://pd.example.com/incidents/INC-2026-345
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created INC-2026-345 (severity: high). Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/inference/runbooks/canary-failures -> paging oncall.
mike (oncall): ack - I'm oncall and looking. Pulling logs + checking canary pool.
sara (sre): seeing lots of 502/503 from canary pods. Error spike aligns with a release roll at 00:12 UTC. Quick snapshot: canary pool nodes showing OOM-ish traces and long tail latencies.
amanda (eng-release): confirming: rolled rollout v1.3.7 -> v1.3.8 canary at 00:10 UTC, traffic ramp to 20% at 00:12. No hotfix yet. Any rate limit/retry changes in this release?
diego (prod-ops): telemetry snippet from metrics (00:08 -> 00:18):
```
canary_error_rate: 1.8% -> 42.3%
median_latency_ms: 120 -> 310
req_rate: 2500/min -> 6100/min
kv_cache_miss: 4% -> 29%
```
mike (oncall): looks strongly correlated. I'm going to divert traffic off canary and scale it to 0 while we investigate. Running traffic command now.
```
# divert all traffic to stable
redwoodctl traffic set inference-api --split stable=100,canary=0 --reason "emergency divert: canary error spike"
```
incident-bot: Action: traffic diversion executed by mike (oncall). Fallback policy applied: stable fallback (100%).
amanda (eng-release): acknowledging - starting rollback of canary to v1.3.6; will also bisect the change that touched tokenization+kv cache handling. ETA ~8m.
sara (sre): grabbing pod logs from canary runtime for 1.3.8, observed repeated `RuntimeError: kv_cache exhausted` and `retry loop exceeded` backtraces. Posting truncated logs: 
```
[00:13:21] runtime: kv cache miss spike, evicting key=0x7f...
[00:13:22] handler: got 502 from upstream inference engine (worker-12)
[00:13:24] retry: requeued request id=abc123, attempts=3
```

mike (oncall): rollback in progress. Notifying VIPs and CS.
emily (support): seeing ~12 new support threads since 00:14 UTC, 8 customers reporting timeouts/errors on generation endpoints. Sending status note to affected customers now. Template: "We're investigating an intermittent issue; engineers are rolling back a recent canary and diverting traffic; ETA for resolution ~15-30m."
amanda (eng-release): rollback to v1.3.6 completed at 00:20 UTC. Canary pods terminated and stable scaled to 100%. Confirming images/pkgs rollback.
diego (prod-ops): metrics after rollback (00:21 UTC):
```
canary_error_rate: -> 0.9%
median_latency_ms: -> 130
req_rate: -> 2600/min
```
sara (sre): system appears healthy, error rate back to baseline. No ongoing elevated 5xx. Rechecks in 5m.
mike (oncall): marking incident as mitigated; creating checklist for postmortem. Assigning followups: amanda -> root cause & fix PR, diego -> improve pre-rollout telemetry guard, sara -> add an automated smoke test for kv cache pressure. emily -> customer follow-up + incident notification.
amanda (eng-release): preliminary root cause: change to tokenization cache/eviction in v1.3.8 interacted poorly with new batching heuristics -> kv cache pressure and eviction storms under realistic traffic. Will open PR to revert tokenization cache change and add unit+load tests.
emily (support): sent customers an update: "We've rolled back the deployment and are monitoring; we'll follow up once we have root cause." Link to status page: https://status.redwood.example/incident/INC-2026-345
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-345 status -> MITIGATED. Time open: ~18m. Postmortem owner assigned: amanda. Slack postmortem thread: #postmortems.
mike (oncall): handing off to amanda for RCA and to emily for customer comms. I'll stay available for 30m in case metrics regress. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
